name: Unbounce
tagline: Create a focused landing-page builder and run a small user-controlled A or B test

pricing.notes: Typical entry monthly tier; packaging changes periodically.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 5 landing pages; 500 unique visitors/month; 1 user; 1 root domain; unlimited conversions and subdomains
tiers.notes: Regular recurring price. Annual billing is charged upfront and advertised as 25% less.

tiers.name: Build
tiers.limits: Unlimited landing pages; 20,000 unique visitors/month; 1 user; 1 root domain; unlimited conversions and subdomains

tiers.name: Experiment
tiers.limits: Unlimited pages, A/B tests and variants; 30,000 unique visitors/month; 3 users; 2 root domains

tiers.name: Optimize
tiers.limits: Unlimited pages; 50,000 unique visitors/month; 5 users; 3 root domains

tiers.name: Concierge
tiers.limits: Starts at 100,000 unique visitors/month, 15 users and 5 root domains; dedicated implementation and success support
tiers.notes: Custom quote and a minimum 12-month commitment, even where installments are monthly.

tiers.name: Agency
tiers.limits: Starts at 50,000 unique visitors/month, 5 users and 10 root domains; client-account and agency controls

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial, generally 1 user with no custom domain and trial traffic restrictions
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-25%); Concierge has a 12-month minimum commitment
pricing.hiddenCosts: $80 for every extra 10,000 unique visitors, or any part of that block, after the included allowance; professional services are separate, and Concierge remains an annual commitment even when paid in installments

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Unbounce, create a focused landing-page builder and run a small user-controlled A or B test. The hard boundary is managed traffic routing, experimentation, integrations, templates, and conversion intelligence, plus editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble responsive landing pages, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, run a small user-controlled A or B test, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
whatYouLose: managed traffic routing, experimentation, integrations, templates, and conversion intelligence
moatNotes: editor polish, hosting, templates, and ecosystem
ongoingBurden: responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Unbounce because the page renderer is reproducible, but customers pay to avoid becoming their own hosting and browser-compatibility team. The recurring cost buys responsive rendering, forms, domains, certificates, deploys, backups, template maintenance, and browser regressions, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Webstudio
priorArt.desc: Open-source visual website builder designed around web standards.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: A focused landing-page stack with forms, analytics and user-controlled A/B tests; you operate every moving part.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Hosted pages, forms and one A/B test free; enough for a small experiment, not an optimization department.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The editor framework is free; the experiment runner, analytics and hosting are imaginary.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Webstudio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A strong page builder with no built-in free experimentation product.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Build plan and a single-site builder DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Unbounce in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and static export; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble responsive landing pages, edit copy and media, preview breakpoints, run a small user-controlled A or B test, and publish a static site to a user-owned target.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Provide a section library for hero, proof, features, pricing, FAQ, and footer blocks.
Use a constrained design-token system rather than arbitrary CSS controls.
Allow inline text editing and local image upload with responsive optimization.
Preview desktop, tablet, and mobile widths and surface overflow errors.
Persist projects in SQLite and support a portable JSON export.
Generate a clean static Next.js output and document deployment to one target.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace.
Deliberately leave out multi-tenant managed hosting.
Deliberately leave out advanced ecommerce, memberships, and agency billing.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
